project.name: morph
project.domain: Real-time deepfake/voice-spoof detection integrated into a live browser-to-browser WebRTC call.
project.goal: Build a demo where one participant's live audio is captured, transmitted through WebRTC, converted to 16 kHz mono Float32 PCM, streamed to a FastAPI detection WebSocket, passed through a replaceable ML model, and surfaced in the frontend as a continuously updating Risk Score plus a temporally gated fake-audio alert.

stack.communications: WebRTC peer-to-peer audio plus WebSocket signaling and WebSocket detection streaming

project.design_principle: Keep the model replaceable. The retrained teammate model should be swappable into the same frontend/backend streaming architecture without redesigning the call system.

temporal_detection_implementation.objective: Eliminate alert popup spam caused by repeated FAKE model windows while preserving a continuously updated raw Risk Score.

entry.raw_gate: Require 3 consecutive raw windows where fake_probability > 0.75.
entry.smoothed_gate: EWMA must reach >= 0.82 to enter FAKE.
entry.transition: REAL -> FAKE produces enteredFake=true exactly once.

exit.condition: When smoothed probability falls to <= 0.55, state can exit FAKE and return to REAL.
exit.purpose: Hysteresis prevents rapid flapping and prevents one low model window from instantly clearing a sustained FAKE state.

implementation.alert_semantics: enteredFake is true only on a REAL -> FAKE transition. Sustained FAKE windows do not retrigger the alert.
implementation.reset: End-call resets detector to pristine REAL state.
implementation.implementation_style: Pure dependency-free TemporalDetector state machine plus a thin React hook using a ref to avoid render forking; process/reset callbacks are stable.

cases.B: 0.9 repeated 3 times -> FAKE on third qualifying window.
cases.B2: Broken raw streak resets the consecutive-window gate.
cases.C: Sustained high windows -> exactly one enteredFake.
cases.D: Smoothed value in approximately 0.55-0.82 holds FAKE.
cases.E: Low stream exits FAKE, with no same-first-window shortcut.
cases.F: After exit, a new qualifying episode can re-enter FAKE and produce exactly one transition.
cases.G: No temporal-detector interaction preserves FAKE without repeated alerts.

risk_score_vs_temporal_state.risk_score: Raw model-facing UI metric. Changes every detection result based on fake_probability.
risk_score_vs_temporal_state.temporal_state: Smoothed decision state used to control alert transitions.
risk_score_vs_temporal_state.important_implication: A high Risk Score does not necessarily mean the popup should immediately appear; the temporal layer intentionally filters alert transitions.

semantic_model_of_key_concepts.return_to_real: The temporal detector is not permanently FAKE. After being in FAKE, sufficiently low smoothed evidence, with hysteresis, allows it to return to REAL. This permits a later distinct suspicious episode to produce another enteredFake event.
semantic_model_of_key_concepts.one_alert_policy: The alert is intended to open once per REAL -> FAKE transition, not once per detection window while the raw model remains FAKE.
semantic_model_of_key_concepts.hysteresis: Use a higher threshold to enter FAKE than to exit FAKE, preventing rapid state flapping.
semantic_model_of_key_concepts.consecutive_gate: Three qualifying raw windows reduce the chance that one isolated high model prediction immediately triggers the alert.
